newsitem.title: UK: British retail sales surge 5.4 percent.
newsitem.headline: British retail sales surge 5.4 percent.

text.p: British retail sales surged 5.4 percent in the year to June, the Office for National Statistics said Wednesday, providing further evidence that interest rates may need to rise again to present a resurgence in inflation.
The ONS said retail sales were up 0.6 percent in June from May levels.
There was an unprecedented 21 percent rise from June, 1996, in sales of household goods.

Economists saw this as evidence that billions of pounds of "windfall" payments that millions of Britons are receiving from the conversion of mutually owned building societies into banks are being spent rather than saved.

"These windfall payments look as though they are going right into the consumer goods sector, particularly the household goods sector," said Stephen Hannah, an economist at IBJ International. "They are not being saved to the extent that was previously thought. This must be something of a worry to the authorities."

Official interest rates have been raised three times in as many months to the present 6.75 percent and many economists believe the Bank of England will raise them again next month to try to dampen consumer demand.
